findings.issue_text: [BUG] addGuests.handler requires isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to both be true, so the check named isTeamAdminOrOwner collapses to owner-only (isTeamAdmin already returns true for owners), and team members holding only the ADMIN role are rejected. A team admin (non-owner) managing a team event's booking clicks 'Additional guests' and gets the FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' error; only the booking's organizer or a team owner can use the feature, contradicting the check's stated intent.

[BUG] BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased when parsed but the filter compares the raw guest email via blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest), so any guest address containing an uppercase letter bypasses the blocklist. With BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS='spam@x.com', a request adding 'SPAM@x.com' passes the filter and the booking's email flow sends ICS REQUESTs and notification emails to an address the operator explicitly blocked.

[BUG] ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts duplicate emails and addGuests.handler's filter only removes guests matching pre-existing attendees (case-sensitively), so one request containing the same email twice creates two Attendee rows for the booking — uniqueness is enforced only in the client dialog's local zod refine, never at the API boundary. A direct tRPC call with guests ['a@b.com','a@b.com'] (or 'A@B.com' plus 'a@b.com') persists duplicate attendee records for the same bookingId, and the duplicated address appears twice in evt.attendees and the ICS attendee list, receiving duplicate emails.

[BUG] addGuests.handler loads the booking with no status filter and BookingListItem adds the 'Additional guests' action to the base menu unconditionally, so guests can be added to CANCELLED or still-PENDING bookings. New guests of a cancelled booking receive an ICS REQUEST with STATUS:CONFIRMED plus a 'Guests Added' email for a meeting that does not exist, updateCalendarAttendees mutates the calendar entry of a cancelled event, and for pending bookings guests are told the event is confirmed before the organizer has accepted it.

[BUG] For event types with seatsPerTimeSlot the handler creates Attendee rows directly with no capacity check and no AttendeeSeatReference, so guests added through this endpoint exceed the booked seat count and exist outside the seat-reference model the seats feature is built on. A seated booking already at capacity gains additional attendees (overbooking the time slot, since seat availability is derived from booking attendees), and seats-driven logic that reads each attendee's seat reference encounters attendees without one.

[BUG] The mutation's onSuccess closes the dialog and resets the email list but never calls setIsInvalidEmail(false), so after a failed validation followed by a successful add, the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner is still rendered the next time the dialog is opened. The user reopening the Add Guests dialog sees a validation error above an empty, valid form until they cancel or submit again; the banner is also never cleared while the user corrects the emails after a failed attempt.

[ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails failures are caught and reduced to console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') with the error object discarded, and the handler still returns success. The organizer sees the 'Guests added' success toast while some or all attendees received nothing, and the log line carries no error detail or structured-logger context, making the failure undiagnosable in production.

[ADVISORY] When every submitted guest is filtered out because they are already an attendee or blacklisted, the handler throws BAD_REQUEST with message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', which is false in both cases. A user adding an already-invited colleague (the dialog only checks uniqueness within the current input, not against existing attendees) is told their emails are invalid instead of 'already invited', prompting confused retries with the same result.

[ADVISORY] The new addGuestsHandler — the permission matrix (organizer/attendee/team admin/owner), dedup and blacklist filtering, the new-guest-vs-existing-attendee email split, and the calendar attendee update — ships with no test in this diff. A regression in any of these branches (e.g., the permission conjunction or the guest filter) reaches production unnoticed, since the only exercise of this logic is manual UI interaction.

[BUG] The permission check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && while naming the result isTeamAdminOrOwner, so team admins who are not owners are denied instead of allowed. A team admin (role ADMIN) who is not the booking's organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's bookings — the admin portion of the intended permission matrix (organizer/admin/owner/attendee) is silently dropped; under exclusive membership roles the && can only ever pass for OWNERs.

[BUG] addGuestsHandler never checks booking.status, and the new 'add_members' action is added to BookingListItem's actions array unconditionally (unlike the ROUND_ROBIN conditional directly below it), so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings. New guests receive AttendeeScheduledEmail invites with a hardcoded status:'CONFIRMED' ics REQUEST (organizer-add-guests-email.ts / attendee-add-guests-email.ts) for an event that was cancelled or never confirmed, re-adding a dead event to their calendars, and existing attendees get 'Guests Added' notices for it.

[BUG] Blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71) but the incoming guest email is compared un-lowercased (line 77), so any case variant of a blacklisted address bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. With BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS='spam@x.com', adding 'Spam@X.com' persists the address as an attendee and emails it a calendar invite replyTo'd to the organizer, defeating the blacklist control entirely.

[BUG] ZAddGuestsInputSchema enforces only per-string email format with no uniqueness, and the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only exact-matches existing attendees, so duplicate or case-variant emails create duplicate Attendee rows. Adding 'John@X.com' when attendee 'john@x.com' already exists — reachable through the dialog, whose uniqueness check only covers the input array — persists a second attendee row for the same person who then receives two different guest emails; a direct API caller can pass the same email twice for the same result.

[BUG] EventManager is constructed from the acting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) even though the permission check deliberately admits non-organizer actors, so for attendee or team-admin actors the calendar update runs without the organizer's calendar credentials. When anyone other than the organizer adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees cannot authenticate against the organizer's destination calendar, so the calendar event's attendee list is never updated (or the mutation errors after attendees were already persisted at line 92), leaving the organizer's calendar and the booking permanently out of sync — the organizer's credentials are already loaded in booking.user.credentials but are not used.

[BUG] For seated event types the handler creates bare Attendee rows via createMany with no seatsPerTimeSlot capacity check and no BookingSeat records, even though it passes seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees into the CalendarEvent (lines 145-146). Guests added to a seated booking exceed the seat limit with no guard, and per-seat flows (seat-only cancellation, sendScheduledSeatsEmails, seat counts on the booking page) never see these attendees because they have no BookingSeat records — the seat-gated sibling path of the attendee model this diff touches was left unchecked.

[BUG] onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never resets isInvalidEmail, so the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error banner persists into the next dialog session. After one failed validation followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog shows the red error banner over a fresh empty form (until Cancel is clicked); the banner also never clears while the user corrects the emails, since nothing resets it on change.

[BUG] The remove-button tooltip uses the hardcoded literal 'Remove email' instead of a t() key, unlike every other user-facing string in the component. Non-English users see an untranslated English tooltip in a shared @calcom/ui component that is exported for reuse beyond this dialog.

[ADVISORY] The new 174-line addGuestsHandler (permission matrix, blacklist filtering, dedup, attendee persistence, calendar update, email fan-out) and the AddGuestsDialog ship with no tests anywhere in this diff — a scan for spec/**, test/**, tests/**, and *.test.*/*.spec.* files in the diff finds none. A regression in the permission check (e.g., the &&/|| logic) or the blacklist filter would silently expose bookings to unauthorized actors or spam addresses with nothing to catch it; the five-actor permission matrix and the filter block are the specific uncovered behaviors worth table-driven tests.

[ADVISORY] Any authenticated attendee may add an unbounded number of guests in a single call (no max on the guests array, no rate limit), and each address receives a calendar invite email replyTo'd to the organizer. An attendee can use an organizer's booking as an invite/email cannon to arbitrary third parties with messages that look like they come from the organizer (phishing surface); the only guard is the global BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env var, which is not per-event-type and is case-broken per the separate bug.

[ADVISORY] The dialog redefines a local ZAddGuestsInputSchema that duplicates the server's addGuests.schema.ts by name but with an extra uniqueness refine the server copy lacks, instead of importing and extending the server schema. The two same-named schemas have already drifted (the server accepts duplicates — see the duplicate-attendee bug), and every future validation rule must be maintained in two places or client and server disagree silently.

[ADVISORY] Email-send failures are caught and reduced to a context-free console.log while the mutation still returns success. An SMTP/provider outage leaves guests persisted with no notifications while the UI reports 'Guests added', and the log line carries no bookingId, recipient count, or error object, so support cannot correlate the silent failure with the booking.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner computes isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), so the flag is only true for team owners and the admin half of its declared admin-or-owner semantics is unreachable. A team admin (non-owner) who is neither organizer nor attendee gets a 403 from addGuests on their team's bookings, so the admin path this flag exists for never works; if isTeamAdmin excludes OWNER, the flag is always false and no team admin/owner other than the organizer can ever add guests via this branch.

[BUG] Neither the handler nor the new BookingListItem action (BookingListItem.tsx:193-200, added unconditionally to the actions array) checks booking.status or start time, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, and past bookings. Adding guests to a cancelled booking emails every attendee an ics REQUEST with status CONFIRMED and runs updateCalendarAttendees against the cancelled event, re-confirming a cancelled meeting on attendees' calendars; the UI exposes this directly from the Cancelled tab of the bookings list.

[BUG] The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71) but the guest email is compared raw (line 77) and the existing-attendee check uses === on raw strings (line 76), so neither comparison is case-normalized. A blacklisted address submitted as 'Spam@X.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and receives the invite, and re-adding an existing attendee with different letter case creates a second Attendee row so that person is emailed twice and appears twice on the calendar event.

[BUG] The server schema omits the uniqueness refine that the client's inline duplicate of this schema enforces (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 re-declares the schema instead of importing it), and the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) does not dedupe within the guests array either. A non-UI client can send guests: ['a@x.com','a@x.com'], which passes server validation and persists two identical Attendee rows via createMany, emailing the same address twice and duplicating it on the calendar event.

[BUG] updateCalendarAttendees runs with the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, even though the authorization block at lines 52-56 explicitly admits non-organizer actors. When anyone other than the organizer triggers addGuests, the calendar update targets a calendar that does not contain the event and silently no-ops or fails, leaving the organizer's Google/Outlook event without the new attendees while the database and emails report them as added.

[BUG] The remove-email tooltip uses the hard-coded literal 'Remove email' instead of t(), the only untranslated user-facing string in the component. Non-English users see an English 'Remove email' tooltip in the add-guests dialog while every surrounding label is localized.

[BUG] isInvalidEmail is set on failed validation but never reset on input change or on the success path (onSuccess at lines 36-41 resets only multiEmailValue), so the error banner outlives the condition that triggered it. After an invalid submit, removing the rows and successfully adding a valid guest leaves isInvalidEmail true, so reopening the dialog shows the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error over an empty form.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint authorizes any booking attendee to add guests, an actor class the UI never exposes (the bookings list is organizer-only), making this API-only capability an expansion not traceable to the stated organizer-facing feature. Any logged-in user who is an attendee on a booking can inject arbitrary email addresses as guests, causing calendar invites (ics REQUEST with reply-to the organizer) to be sent to addresses they choose — an invite-injection vector the organizer-centric requirement does not call for.

[BUG] For event types with seatsPerTimeSlot the handler creates plain Attendee rows via createMany without creating BookingSeat records or routing through the seat-booking flow, even though it copies seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees into the CalendarEvent (lines 145-146). On seated event types the new guest consumes no seat (the slot still shows as available) and seat-scoped attendee handling is skipped, so the booking's seat occupancy and its attendee list disagree.

[ADVISORY] Email send failures are swallowed with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') — the error object is not logged and no failure is surfaced to the caller. When the mail provider call fails, the user still sees the 'Guests added' success toast and the log line contains no diagnostic detail, so operators cannot determine why guests never received invites.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds no tests for the new handler's permission matrix (organizer/team-admin/attendee/outsider), blacklist filtering, or duplicate-guest handling — all new non-trivial logic introduced here. A regression in the authorization or filtering conditions ships silently; the admin-vs-owner operator mistake at lines 46-48 is exactly the class of defect a permission-matrix test would have caught, and a future authz regression would let unauthorized users mutate bookings.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner computes isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId) && isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId), an AND that contradicts its own name, so a team admin who is not the owner (or an owner who is not an admin) evaluates false and is rejected. Team admins/owners who are not both roles get FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's bookings unless they happen to also be the organizer or an attendee; the feature the variable name promises is denied to exactly the staff roles it was built for.

[BUG] The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (lines 26-29) enforces, and the handler's filter (lines 74-78) only dedups against existing attendees, never within the submitted batch. A direct API call with guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] passes validation and createMany inserts two Attendee rows for the same person on the same booking; the invariant exists only in one client's UI and any other caller (API consumer, future client, the two already-drifted copies) silently corrupts the attendee list.

[BUG] The existing-attendee dedup compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively while attendee emails are stored exactly as entered, so the write path and the compare path disagree on canonical form. Re-adding an existing attendee with different casing (John@X.com vs john@x.com) passes the filter, creating a duplicate Attendee row for the same person, who then receives both a full AttendeeScheduledEmail (as a 'new' guest) and an AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (as an existing one) for the same event.

[BUG] The EventManager that executes updateCalendarAttendees is built from the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) while the calendar event being mutated belongs to the booking organizer. For the attendee and team-admin callers the permission model explicitly admits (lines 46-56), the calendar update runs without the organizer's calendar credentials, so the external calendar event is never updated with the new guests — the feature's core promise silently half-fails for every non-organizer caller the design intentionally supports.

[BUG] The booking is fetched by id alone with no status guard anywhere in the handler, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings, and the new emails (attendee-add-guests-email.ts, organizer-add-guests-email.ts) attach an ICS REQUEST with STATUS:CONFIRMED. Adding guests to a cancelled booking sends every attendee a REQUEST/CONFIRMED iCalendar payload that re-confirms the cancelled event in their calendar clients, resurrecting an event the organizer cancelled; the action button is also rendered unconditionally in BookingListItem, so cancelled bookings in the list are one click away from this path.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, while its parameter is named newGuests and used as newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to pick the email class. When a submission mixes an already-existing attendee with a new one (uniqueGuests non-empty so no BAD_REQUEST), the existing attendee matches inside sendAddGuestsEmails and receives a duplicate full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added notice or nothing.

[ADVISORY] The guests array has no maxItems bound and each invocation emails every existing attendee plus every team member, so request cost is unbounded in input size and grows with the attendee list. A single request can create thousands of Attendee rows and fan out thousands of emails plus calendar API calls inside one mutation; adding guests one at a time to a large booking resends the full attendee/team email set per invocation, an O(N²) email pattern operators will see as slow requests and mail-provider rate limits.

[ADVISORY] The dedup-then-insert is a check-then-createMany sequence outside any transaction with no UNIQUE(bookingId, email) constraint on Attendee to backstop it. Two concurrent add-guests requests carrying the same email both read the pre-insert attendee list, both pass the filter, and both insert, producing duplicate attendee rows even with byte-identical casing; only a schema-level unique index (absent) can make the invariant hold under concurrency.

[ADVISORY] The operation is a three-step sequence (DB commit at line 92, external calendar update at line 165, email fan-out at line 168) with no transactional coupling or compensation between steps. If updateCalendarAttendees throws after the attendee rows are committed, the caller sees an error toast but the guests are persisted; retrying the identical submission now hits uniqueGuests.length === 0 and is rejected with BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', stranding the user in a state where the error message is false and the action cannot be retried.

[ADVISORY] For seated event types the handler creates bare Attendee rows via createMany with no corresponding BookingSeat records, even though it reads seatsPerTimeSlot into the CalendarEvent two lines later. On event types with seatsPerTimeSlot set, guests added through this path bypass the seat model that governs capacity and attendee management for that subtype, so seat accounting and any seat-scoped reads diverge from the attendee list this mutation creates.

[ADVISORY] The ~25-line CalendarEvent assembly (organizer/attendee translation resolution, destinationCalendar fallback chain, video reference extraction) duplicates the equivalent block in editLocation.handler rather than sharing an evt-builder. The next change to CalendarEvent's required shape or to destination-calendar resolution must be replicated in every hand-copied handler or the mutation paths silently drift, which is exactly how the userPrimaryEmail-vs-organizer.email fallback here will diverge from its siblings.

[ADVISORY] booking.userId || 0 feeds 0 into findFirstOrThrow when the booking has no userId, converting a nullable-organizer booking into a guaranteed miss. A booking with a null userId makes the mutation throw an unhandled Prisma not-found error (500) instead of a graceful NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN response; the || 0 sentinel exists only to satisfy the type, not to handle the case it silences.

[BUG] The team-staff permission check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with '&&' even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner; since a team membership holds a single role, the admin-or-owner grant collapses to owner-only (or to nothing, if isTeamAdmin excludes OWNER). A team ADMIN who is not the booking's organizer and not an attendee receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's booking; the feature's access objective was silently narrowed from 'admins or owners' to 'owners only', and both membership queries always execute even when the first is false.

[BUG] addGuestsHandler loads the booking by id alone and never checks booking.status, and the new list action (BookingListItem.tsx:193-200) is offered unconditionally, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-past bookings. New guests on a cancelled or unconfirmed booking receive calendar REQUEST invites with status CONFIRMED plus 'Guests Added' emails for a meeting that was cancelled or never accepted, misleading them into showing up; the happy-path assumption 'existing booking = active booking' was never validated against the data model.

[BUG] The server schema accepts duplicate emails (z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refinement) while the dialog's hand-copied schema (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29) enforces uniqueness only client-side, and the handler's filter dedupes only against existing attendees, never within the input array. A direct API call with ['a@b.com','a@b.com'] creates two Attendee rows for the same address and sends that person two 'booking confirmed' emails with a duplicated calendar attendee list; the client and server schemas are parallel hand-maintained copies that have already drifted.

[BUG] The dedupe and blacklist filter compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email, blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)) even though the blacklist entries are lowercased at lines 70-71. Adding 'User@X.com' when 'user@x.com' already attends creates a second Attendee row for the same person with duplicate notification emails, and the same casing trick bypasses the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS control entirely.

[BUG] EventManager is constructed from the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking owner's, even though the query at lines 35-40 fetches booking.user.credentials, so updateCalendarAttendees runs against whatever calendar connections the caller happens to have. When a permitted attendee (line 54) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees cannot resolve the organizer's calendar connection from the caller's credential set, so the organizer's calendar event is left without the new attendees while the DB write and success-path emails proceed — the calendar silently diverges from the booking record.

[BUG] The attendee DB write (lines 92-106) is followed by an unguarded 'await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees', so any calendar API failure rejects the mutation after the guests are already persisted. An expired calendar token turns the add into a 500 after partial persistence: attendees exist in the database but received no invite, and a retry with the same emails is rejected with BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', stranding the user in a state the UI cannot represent.

[BUG] The handler passes seatsPerTimeSlot through to the calendar event but performs no seat-capacity check and creates plain Attendee rows without seat records, so seated event types accept unlimited extra guests. A seated event type with seatsPerTimeSlot=1 that is fully booked gains any number of additional attendees via addGuests, each receiving calendar invites, while seat accounting never increments — the slot is overbooked outside the seat system.

[BUG] onSuccess resets the email list and closes the dialog but never clears isInvalidEmail, so the error banner set by a failed validation attempt survives into the next open of the dialog. Reopening the add-guests dialog for the same booking shows the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner over an empty form with no invalid input present.

[ADVISORY] Blacklisted emails are silently filtered out of the guest list while the handler still returns success. An operator maintaining BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS gets no signal, and the acting user sees the 'Guests added' toast while the blacklisted address was never added — a silent partial application of the requested action.

[ADVISORY] Email dispatch failures are swallowed with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'), discarding the error object and bypassing the structured logger. In production an email-provider outage is invisible: users get the success toast, no attendee is notified, and support has no error detail to diagnose with because the caught error is never logged.

[ADVISORY] The same error key emails_must_be_unique_valid is thrown when every input email is already an attendee or blacklisted, reusing the client's invalid-input message for a semantically different failure. A user adding an email that already attends is told 'Emails must be unique and valid' even though they entered one valid, unique address, sending them hunting for a formatting problem that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] The remove-guest tooltip uses the hardcoded literal 'Remove email' in an otherwise fully localized component. Every non-English locale shows an English tooltip on the remove button of the new shared MultiEmail control used in the guest dialog.

[ADVISORY] The new 174-line handler ships with no test covering its three-way permission matrix, the dedupe/blacklist filter, or the DB-then-calendar-then-email ordering. The '&&' permission defect and the case-sensitive dedupe both reached the diff unnoticed precisely because no test exercises them; any future refactor of this authorization and dedupe logic lands equally unverified.

[BUG] The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blocklist is lowercased at load time but compared against raw-case guest input via case-sensitive includes, so any case variation bypasses the blocklist. With BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS='spam@evil.com', a caller submits 'SPAM@evil.com'; blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) is false, the attendee row is created and invite emails are sent to the blacklisted address, defeating the abuse control the env var exists for.

[ADVISORY] guests: z.array(z.string().email()) has no maximum length, so a single addGuests mutation accepts an unbounded email list. One authenticated call from an organizer or attendee creates thousands of attendee rows via createMany, fires thousands of outbound emails in sendAddGuestsEmails, and pushes the full list into updateCalendarAttendees — a one-request spam/DoS amplifier that burns the sender's mail reputation and the organizer's calendar API quota, with no cap or rate limit anywhere in the path.

[BUG] addGuestsHandler appends attendees without consulting eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot capacity or the booking's payment state, so guests added through this endpoint bypass seat accounting entirely. On a paid per-seat event type, an organizer or attendee adds any number of guests via the mutation; each receives the calendar invite and meeting link without a seat record or payment, bypassing the per-seat revenue and capacity limits enforced at booking time.

[BUG] The server schema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client dialog enforces (AddGuestsDialog.tsx refine on Set size), and the handler's filter dedupes only against existing attendees with a case-sensitive comparison, so duplicate guests within one request are accepted. A direct call to trpc.viewer.bookings.addGuests with guests ['a@b.com','a@b.com'] (or 'A@b.com' when 'a@b.com' is already an attendee) inserts duplicate attendee rows for the same person and sends duplicate invite emails; only the client-side Set check prevents this for UI users, so any non-UI caller corrupts the attendee list.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner combines the admin and owner role checks with &&, requiring the caller to hold both roles simultaneously, so a team admin who is not the team owner is denied despite the check's name and the feature's team path. Team admins get FORBIDDEN on team bookings they administer; the defect fails closed (no over-grant), but the team-authorization path of the feature is dead for admins and the misleading name invites an unreviewed flip to || later.

[ADVISORY] The handler never validates booking.status before appending guests and sending mail, while the new email templates hardcode ICS status CONFIRMED with method REQUEST. Guests added to a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking (or an already-past one) receive CONFIRMED calendar invites that resurrect the cancelled meeting in their calendars — an attendee can keep emitting confirmed-looking invites from a dead booking (packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts:15).

[ADVISORY] updateCalendarAttendees is executed with the caller's own credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, so a non-organizer caller's calendar credentials are used against the organizer's destination calendar event. When an attendee adds guests, the organizer's calendar event is never updated — the DB attendee rows are already committed at line 92-106, so the caller either gets a 500 after a partial write (retry creates duplicate attendees) or a silent calendar/DB divergence.

[ADVISORY] The authorization disjunction grants any authenticated user whose email exactly matches an existing attendee the right to append guests to the booking, not just the organizer. A booking participant with a Cal.com account can unilaterally add arbitrary addresses that then receive method:REQUEST calendar invites and the meeting's video-call details under the organizer's identity; the organizer's only visibility is a single summary email after the sends have already gone out.

[BUG] Email send failures are silently swallowed: sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped in a try/catch whose body is only `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` — the caught error object is not even logged — and the handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` as success. New guests never receive the calendar invite/ICS email while the organizer sees a 'Guests added' success toast; the dropped notifications are invisible to users, and the single log line contains no error detail, so operators cannot diagnose the failure either.

[BUG] `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs with no error handling after `prisma.booking.update` (lines 92-106) has already committed the new attendees, so a calendar API failure throws a 500 after the DB write — and the retry path is bricked, because the attendee-existence filter (lines 74-78) then reduces uniqueGuests to zero and returns BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. One transient Google/Outlook API error leaves the booking's attendee list permanently out of sync with the calendar event: the user sees an error toast, every retry fails with a misleading validation error (the emails ARE unique and valid — they are already attendees), and no code path can ever push the guests to the calendar.

[BUG] The server schema has no uniqueness constraint — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no refine and no max — and the handler's filter (lines 74-78) only dedupes against existing attendees, not within the input array, so `guests: ["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` passes validation and createMany inserts two attendee rows for the same email. Any direct API caller creates duplicate attendee records, sends duplicate emails, and double-lists the address in ICS recipients; the uniqueness check exists only in a locally re-declared client-side schema inside AddGuestsDialog.tsx (lines 26-29), a hand-maintained copy that has already drifted from the server schema it duplicates.

[BUG] `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner — a conjunction that can never authorize a team admin (a membership holds a single role, so under any role semantics the AND excludes admins), contradicting the 'AdminOrOwner' name that signals `||`. Team admins (and under strict ADMIN-only/OWNER-only helpers, owners too) who are not the organizer or an existing attendee receive FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' when adding guests to their team's bookings, making the team-management path of this feature unreachable for exactly the users it names.

[BUG] The calendar update is built from the acting user's credentials — `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` feeds the EventManager while the organizer's credentials loaded via `booking.user.credentials` (lines 35-39) are never used — so when an attendee or team admin adds guests, the credential lookup against booking.references misses or authenticates as the wrong account, and the calendar event is not updated. Non-organizer actors get a 'Guests added' success response while the real calendar event keeps its old attendee list (silent partial success), or the mismatched-credential update throws into the unguarded path at line 165 and 500s after the DB commit.


therefore excludes team admins who are not owners (and not organizer/attendee), matching the finding that the intended “admin OR owner” permission is silently dropped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` definitions with the same name in different layers: the client dialog defines `const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, enforcing uniqueness, while the server schema in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` is `z.object({ bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email()) })` and does not enforce uniqueness. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/contract-consistency issue (client/server validation rules can drift), though it’s not inherently a guaranteed runtime defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Email-send failures are caught and reduced to a context-free console.log while the mutation still returns success. An SMTP/provider outage leaves guests persisted with no notifications while the UI reports 'Guests added', and the log line carries no bookingId, recipient count, or error object, so support cannot correlate the silent failure with the booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation updates/persists attendees and calendar (`prisma.booking.update`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`) and then wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and discards the caught `err`, with no bookingId/guest count context, while still returning `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This matches the finding’s claim about silent email-send failures and context-free logging; however, it’s not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone because the core action (adding guests) still succeeds and email is a side-effect that may be intentionally best-effort.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner computes isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), so the flag is only true for team owners and the admin half of its declared admin-or-owner semantics is unreachable. A team admin (non-owner) who is neither organizer nor attendee gets a 403 from addGuests on their team's bookings, so the admin path this flag exists for never works; if isTeamAdmin excludes OWNER, the flag is always false and no team admin/owner other than the organizer can ever add guests via this branch.
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that isTeamAdminOrOwner uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, making the admin-or-owner intent unreachable for admins who aren’t owners (and potentially always false). This is the same core bug as the golden comment: it should be an OR condition, not AND, because permission should be granted if the user is either admin or owner.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Neither the handler nor the new BookingListItem action (BookingListItem.tsx:193-200, added unconditionally to the actions array) checks booking.status or start time, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, and past bookings. Adding guests to a cancelled booking emails every attendee an ics REQUEST with status CONFIRMED and runs updateCalendarAttendees against the cancelled event, re-confirming a cancelled meeting on attendees' calendars; the UI exposes this directly from the Cancelled tab of the bookings list.

adjudication.rationale: The new BookingListItem action `add_members` is added to the `actions` array unconditionally (no guard on booking status or start/end time) and simply opens `AddGuestsDialog`. On the server, `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking by `id` and performs permission checks but does not check `booking.status` (or any time-based constraint) before mutating attendees and calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. The new email templates generate an ICS REQUEST with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`packages/emails/templates/*add-guests-email.ts`), so for cancelled/rejected/past bookings this could incorrectly update calendars and send "confirmed" ICS updates. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71) but the guest email is compared raw (line 77) and the existing-attendee check uses === on raw strings (line 76), so neither comparison is case-normalized. A blacklisted address submitted as 'Spam@X.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and receives the invite, and re-adding an existing attendee with different letter case creates a second Attendee row so that person is emailed twice and appears twice on the calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased (`split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but `uniqueGuests` filters with `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` using the raw `guest` string from input, so mixed-case submissions can bypass the blacklist. Similarly, the duplicate check `!booking.attendees.some(attendee => guest === attendee.email)` is a raw string equality check, so `Spam@X.com` vs `spam@x.com` would not be detected as an existing attendee and could be inserted via `createMany`, resulting in duplicate attendee rows/emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The server schema omits the uniqueness refine that the client's inline duplicate of this schema enforces (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 re-declares the schema instead of importing it), and the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) does not dedupe within the guests array either. A non-UI client can send guests: ['a@x.com','a@x.com'], which passes server validation and persists two identical Attendee rows via createMany, emailing the same address twice and duplicating it on the calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness, while the client dialog re-declares a stricter schema with a uniqueness `refine` (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx) that can be bypassed by non-UI callers. In the handler, `uniqueGuests` is computed via `guests.filter(...)` against existing attendees and a blacklist (addGuests.handler.ts), but it does not dedupe within the provided `guests` array itself, so an input like `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` can produce duplicate entries in `guestsFullDetails` and be persisted via `attendees.createMany`. This can lead to duplicated attendee rows and repeated downstream effects (e.g., sending multiple emails / calendar attendee updates) based on the duplicated attendees list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateCalendarAttendees runs with the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, even though the authorization block at lines 52-56 explicitly admits non-organizer actors. When anyone other than the organizer triggers addGuests, the calendar update targets a calendar that does not contain the event and silently no-ops or fails, leaving the organizer's Google/Outlook event without the new attendees while the database and emails report them as added.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly permits non-organizer callers (`isAttendee` / team admin/owner) but then builds `EventManager` using `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the caller) and spreads `...user` (caller identity) before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The booking’s organizer is `booking.userId`, and the handler even fetches `organizer` separately, but never uses organizer credentials. This makes the calendar update depend on the caller’s calendar integrations, which for non-organizers will often not contain the event, so the external calendar may not get updated while DB + emails proceed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The remove-email tooltip uses the hard-coded literal 'Remove email' instead of t(), the only untranslated user-facing string in the component. Non-English users see an English 'Remove email' tooltip in the add-guests dialog while every surrounding label is localized.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the remove button tooltip is hard-coded as `content="Remove email"` while the component otherwise uses `t()` (e.g., `t("add_another")`) and the dialog passes localized labels. This introduces an English-only user-facing string for non-English locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isInvalidEmail is set on failed validation but never reset on input change or on the success path (onSuccess at lines 36-41 resets only multiEmailValue), so the error banner outlives the condition that triggered it. After an invalid submit, removing the rows and successfully adding a valid guest leaves isInvalidEmail true, so reopening the dialog shows the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error over an empty form.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation in `handleAdd`, but it is not reset in the mutation `onSuccess` handler (which only calls `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])`). Since the dialog component is always mounted from `BookingListItem` and `Dialog` open/close does not unmount it, reopening after a previous invalid submit can still render the error banner over an empty/reset form. `isInvalidEmail` is only reset on the Cancel button path, not on successful add or general close.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The endpoint authorizes any booking attendee to add guests, an actor class the UI never exposes (the bookings list is organizer-only), making this API-only capability an expansion not traceable to the stated organizer-facing feature. Any logged-in user who is an attendee on a booking can inject arbitrary email addresses as guests, causing calendar invites (ics REQUEST with reply-to the organizer) to be sent to addresses they choose — an invite-injection vector the organizer-centric requirement does not call for.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly authorizes any existing booking attendee to add more guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and access is allowed when `isAttendee` is true (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). This means any logged-in attendee on a booking can call `viewer.bookings.addGuests` and cause new attendee records to be created (`attendees.createMany`) and calendar/email notifications to be sent (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`), enabling invite injection to arbitrary emails beyond organizer/team control.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] For event types with seatsPerTimeSlot the handler creates plain Attendee rows via createMany without creating BookingSeat records or routing through the seat-booking flow, even though it copies seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees into the CalendarEvent (lines 145-146). On seated event types the new guest consumes no seat (the slot still shows as available) and seat-scoped attendee handling is skipped, so the booking's seat occupancy and its attendee list disagree.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation adds new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { ... }}}})` without any seat-capacity enforcement or any seat-specific persistence/flow (no branching on `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`). Yet the handler later sets `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` on the `CalendarEvent` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot`, `evt.seatsShowAttendees`) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, implying seated events are supported but not handled here. From this diff alone, adding guests to a seated event can bypass seat limits and make booking attendee state inconsistent with seat availability/occupancy mechanisms.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Email send failures are swallowed with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') — the error object is not logged and no failure is surfaced to the caller. When the mail provider call fails, the user still sees the 'Guests added' success toast and the log line contains no diagnostic detail, so operators cannot determine why guests never received invites.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which discards `err` and always returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This means email provider failures produce no diagnostic detail and are not surfaced to the caller/UI (the UI success toast is triggered on mutation success), even though the primary action (adding guests to the booking) did succeed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds no tests for the new handler's permission matrix (organizer/team-admin/attendee/outsider), blacklist filtering, or duplicate-guest handling — all new non-trivial logic introduced here. A regression in the authorization or filtering conditions ships silently; the admin-vs-owner operator mistake at lines 46-48 is exactly the class of defect a permission-matrix test would have caught, and a future authz regression would let unauthorized users mutate bookings.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new non-trivial mutation path (`viewer.bookings.addGuests`), including permission checks, blacklist filtering, and deduping/uniqueness handling in `addGuests.handler.ts`, but the diff adds no accompanying tests for those behaviors. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap given the new authorization/filtering logic. The handler also contains a likely logical mistake in `isTeamAdminOrOwner` (computed with `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` while the name implies an OR), which is exactly the kind of issue a permission-matrix test would catch, reinforcing the importance of adding tests here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner computes isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId) && isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId), an AND that contradicts its own name, so a team admin who is not the owner (or an owner who is not an admin) evaluates false and is rejected. Team admins/owners who are not both roles get FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's bookings unless they happen to also be the organizer or an attendee; the feature the variable name promises is denied to exactly the staff roles it was built for.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with an AND: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This contradicts the variable name and likely intended authorization logic (admin OR owner). The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will reject team admins who are not owners (and owners who are not admins) from adding guests unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (lines 26-29) enforces, and the handler's filter (lines 74-78) only dedups against existing attendees, never within the submitted batch. A direct API call with guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] passes validation and createMany inserts two Attendee rows for the same person on the same booking; the invariant exists only in one client's UI and any other caller (API consumer, future client, the two already-drifted copies) silently corrupts the attendee list.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness like the client-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` (refine with `Set`). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed via `guests.filter(...)` only excluding emails already present in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not dedupe duplicates within the submitted `guests` array. Therefore an API call with `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` can pass validation and result in `createMany` inserting duplicate attendee rows for the same booking (no uniqueness constraint shown in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The existing-attendee dedup compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively while attendee emails are stored exactly as entered, so the write path and the compare path disagree on canonical form. Re-adding an existing attendee with different casing (John@X.com vs john@x.com) passes the filter, creating a duplicate Attendee row for the same person, who then receives both a full AttendeeScheduledEmail (as a 'new' guest) and an AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (as an existing one) for the same event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees via `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, which is case-sensitive and does not canonicalize emails. Since attendee emails are stored as-entered (`createMany` uses `email: guest`), adding the same address with different casing can bypass the filter and create a duplicate attendee row. This also impacts `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`: it checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` case-sensitively, so the original-cased attendee and the newly inserted differently cased attendee can receive different email templates (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail vs AttendeeScheduledEmail), resulting in two emails to what is effectively the same mailbox.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The EventManager that executes updateCalendarAttendees is built from the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) while the calendar event being mutated belongs to the booking organizer. For the attendee and team-admin callers the permission model explicitly admits (lines 46-56), the calendar update runs without the organizer's calendar credentials, so the external calendar event is never updated with the new guests — the feature's core promise silently half-fails for every non-organizer caller the design intentionally supports.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission model allows non-organizers (team admin/owner and attendees) to call `addGuestsHandler` (checks around `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isOrganizer`, `isAttendee`). However the external calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, i.e., using the *calling user’s* credentials, not the booking organizer’s (`booking.userId` / `booking.user.credentials` is already loaded but unused). Since the calendar event being updated corresponds to the booking/organizer’s calendar integration, non-organizer callers are likely to lack the necessary organizer calendar credentials, causing `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` to fail to update the external event (and the code does not handle/report that failure). This matches the finding’s claim of a silent core-feature failure for allowed non-organizer callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The booking is fetched by id alone with no status guard anywhere in the handler, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings, and the new emails (attendee-add-guests-email.ts, organizer-add-guests-email.ts) attach an ICS REQUEST with STATUS:CONFIRMED. Adding guests to a cancelled booking sends every attendee a REQUEST/CONFIRMED iCalendar payload that re-confirms the cancelled event in their calendar clients, resurrecting an event the organizer cancelled; the action button is also rendered unconditionally in BookingListItem, so cancelled bookings in the list are one click away from this path.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and there is no check on any booking status/state before updating attendees and sending emails. The new email templates (`packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) generate an ICS payload with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"`, so invoking this on a cancelled/rejected booking would still send a CONFIRMED REQUEST update. Additionally, the UI action is added unconditionally in `BookingListItem` (the `add_members` action is always present), making it reachable from the list regardless of booking state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, while its parameter is named newGuests and used as newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to pick the email class. When a submission mixes an already-existing attendee with a new one (uniqueGuests non-empty so no BAD_REQUEST), the existing attendee matches inside sendAddGuestsEmails and receives a duplicate full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added notice or nothing.
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core bug: sendAddGuestsEmails iterates over the full calendarEvent.attendees list but decides which email to send using newGuests.includes(attendee.email), where newGuests corresponds to the (raw) input guests rather than the actual newly-added/unique guests. This mismatch can cause existing attendees to be treated as “new” and receive the wrong/duplicate email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The guests array has no maxItems bound and each invocation emails every existing attendee plus every team member, so request cost is unbounded in input size and grows with the attendee list. A single request can create thousands of Attendee rows and fan out thousands of emails plus calendar API calls inside one mutation; adding guests one at a time to a large booking resends the full attendee/team email set per invocation, an O(N²) email pattern operators will see as slow requests and mail-provider rate limits.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows unbounded input and fan-out work: ZAddGuestsInputSchema allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no max, and `addGuestsHandler` does `attendees.createMany` for all `uniqueGuests` (no cap). It then builds `evt.attendees` from *all* booking attendees (`bookingAttendees.attendees.map(...)`) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` plus `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, where `sendAddGuestsEmails` emails the organizer, each team member, and then maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` to send an email per attendee. This means each invocation’s cost grows with current attendee list, and repeated “add guests” calls will repeatedly email the full attendee set (quadratic total over many invocations). This is a concrete, diff-grounded scalability/operational-risk concern rather than a clearly incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dedup-then-insert is a check-then-createMany sequence outside any transaction with no UNIQUE(bookingId, email) constraint on Attendee to backstop it. Two concurrent add-guests requests carrying the same email both read the pre-insert attendee list, both pass the filter, and both insert, producing duplicate attendee rows even with byte-identical casing; only a schema-level unique index (absent) can make the invariant hold under concurrency.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the code reads the booking + current attendees (`prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`), computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that snapshot, then does a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }})`. This is a classic check-then-insert sequence with no transaction or `skipDuplicates`, so concurrent requests could both pass the pre-check and attempt to insert the same email for the same booking. However, the finding’s claim that there is definitively no `UNIQUE(bookingId, email)` constraint on the Attendee table cannot be verified from this diff (no Prisma schema/migration shown), so the severity as a guaranteed bug is not fully provable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The operation is a three-step sequence (DB commit at line 92, external calendar update at line 165, email fan-out at line 168) with no transactional coupling or compensation between steps. If updateCalendarAttendees throws after the attendee rows are committed, the caller sees an error toast but the guests are persisted; retrying the identical submission now hits uniqueGuests.length === 0 and is rejected with BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', stranding the user in a state where the error message is false and the action cannot be retried.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` before calling the external side effect `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. That calendar update is not wrapped in a try/catch and there is no transaction/compensation with the prior DB write, so if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation fails (client will show an error), but the guests remain added in the DB. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering against `booking.attendees` (re-fetched at the start of the handler), so the same emails are now considered already present and `uniqueGuests.length === 0` triggers a `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, preventing a retry and producing a misleading error. This broken retry semantics and inconsistent state is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] For seated event types the handler creates bare Attendee rows via createMany with no corresponding BookingSeat records, even though it reads seatsPerTimeSlot into the CalendarEvent two lines later. On event types with seatsPerTimeSlot set, guests added through this path bypass the seat model that governs capacity and attendee management for that subtype, so seat accounting and any seat-scoped reads diverge from the attendee list this mutation creates.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation always appends to booking.attendees via prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}}) with no conditional logic around booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot / seatsShowAttendees, even though those fields are propagated into the CalendarEvent immediately afterward. The finding’s specific claim about missing BookingSeat records isn’t directly verifiable from this diff (no BookingSeat model is referenced here), but it is diff-grounded that seated/capacity-related metadata exists and this path doesn’t do any seat/capacity accounting or specialized persistence beyond creating Attendee rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The ~25-line CalendarEvent assembly (organizer/attendee translation resolution, destinationCalendar fallback chain, video reference extraction) duplicates the equivalent block in editLocation.handler rather than sharing an evt-builder. The next change to CalendarEvent's required shape or to destination-calendar resolution must be replicated in every hand-copied handler or the mutation paths silently drift, which is exactly how the userPrimaryEmail-vs-organizer.email fallback here will diverge from its siblings.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a sizable CalendarEvent construction block in `addGuests.handler.ts` (organizer/attendee translations, destinationCalendar fallback, video reference extraction). However, the finding’s core claim is that this block *duplicates* an equivalent block in `editLocation.handler` and will drift from its “siblings” (including a `userPrimaryEmail` vs `organizer.email` fallback difference). The diff does not include `editLocation.handler` (or any other handler) for comparison, so duplication/drift across handlers cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] booking.userId || 0 feeds 0 into findFirstOrThrow when the booking has no userId, converting a nullable-organizer booking into a guaranteed miss. A booking with a null userId makes the mutation throw an unhandled Prisma not-found error (500) instead of a graceful NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN response; the || 0 sentinel exists only to satisfy the type, not to handle the case it silences.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined` (which the `|| 0` explicitly allows), this forces an ID of `0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw, resulting in an unhandled exception (500) rather than a controlled `TRPCError` response. The diff shows no guard for `booking.userId` being null before this call and no try/catch around this query, so the failure mode described is directly supported by the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The team-staff permission check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with '&&' even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner; since a team membership holds a single role, the admin-or-owner grant collapses to owner-only (or to nothing, if isTeamAdmin excludes OWNER). A team ADMIN who is not the booking's organizer and not an attendee receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's booking; the feature's access objective was silently narrowed from 'admins or owners' to 'owners only', and both membership queries always execute even when the first is false.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This contradicts the variable name and typical intended authorization of “admin OR owner”; it effectively requires both predicates to be true, which can narrow access (e.g., admins blocked unless `isTeamAdmin` also returns true for owners and vice-versa). Additionally, both async membership checks always execute even if the first is false. This can cause legitimate team admins (who are neither organizer nor attendee) to hit the `FORBIDDEN` path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] addGuestsHandler loads the booking by id alone and never checks booking.status, and the new list action (BookingListItem.tsx:193-200) is offered unconditionally, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-past bookings. New guests on a cancelled or unconfirmed booking receive calendar REQUEST invites with status CONFIRMED plus 'Guests Added' emails for a meeting that was cancelled or never accepted, misleading them into showing up; the happy-path assumption 'existing booking = active booking' was never validated against the data model.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched solely by `id` (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) and the mutation proceeds to update attendees, update external calendars, and send emails without any check on booking state (no `booking.status`/cancellation/rejection/pending) or even temporal validity (past start/end).
